_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: near_eastern (akkadian) backbone + classical (hellenic) substrate (cross-family fusion, Mesopotamian-leaning)

blend.backbone: near_eastern (akkadian: the alu/bit river-cities, the sangu temple-priesthood, construct-chain toponyms, emphatic gutturals q/kh/sh/', -u/-tu/-um endings, SOV agglutinative grammar, penultimate stress)
blend.substrate: classical (hellenic: the polis and agora, the strategos and the phalanx, sea and learned/civic vocabulary, -os/-on endings, aspirates th/ph/kh)
blend.lean: Mesopotamian-heavy - a Hellenistic dynasty (a Seleucid house) seated on the Akkadian temple-cities of the Two Rivers: Greek learning, the polis, and the gymnasion grafted onto the ziggurat and the law-stele. The Akkadian temple-city and its scribal-priesthood remain the backbone; the Greek register supplies sea, civic, learned, and material words.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_03 Shinarur (Mesopotamian) x BASE_07 (Hellenic/Classical). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: both parents are Civilized (feudal), so Hellashur is Civilized (feudal). Concept: Hellenistic Mesopotamia - a Seleucid Babylon. A Greek conqueror-dynasty took the river-valley temple-cities of the Two Rivers and ruled them in Hellenistic fashion, founding poleis beside the ziggurats, but the Akkadian temple-city endured beneath and supplied the deeper register. Backbone/lean = Akkadian (the alu-cities, the bit-ili temples, the construct-chain toponyms, the scribal-priestly populace, the rule/kin/temple/land vocabulary); substrate = Hellenic (the polis and agora, the strategos, the phalanx, the sea, the learned and material words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Akkadian and Greek registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Akkadian reflexes primary, Hellenic variants secondary), never real gods. The approved foreign term 'Archon' (Greek polis-magistrate) is the English display ruler at the county tier (see approved_foreign_terms_used); all other display titles are English, with the Akkadian conlang forms in ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. All human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic.

phonology.palette: Akkadian backbone - emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, a/i/u vowels, -u/-tu/-um endings, penultimate stress, mimation, construct chains - meeting a Hellenic substrate: vowel-rich (a e i o u), aspirates th/ph/kh, sibilant s, liquids l/r, -os/-on/-e endings, moderate onset clusters (st, tr, pr, kl, sp). Per the CSV: complex consonants over deep vowels, the Akkadian emphatics dominant with the Greek aspirates and clusters retained as a learned overlay; grammar is SOV with agglutinative verb aspects (the Akkadian backbone), the Greek roots fitted to Akkadian stems. Theophoric on the Akkadian construct reflexes (Tullaru-, Urlandu-) with Hellenic morph variants (Tulrio-, Orlandro-) for the learned register.
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Akkadian construct-chains and mimation -um meeting Greek clusters (st, pr, kl, ph, th); penultimate stress; the Greek -os/-on endings adapted toward Akkadian -u or dropped to a consonant-final root; -polis surviving as a learned suffix beside the Bit-/Dur-/Kar- construct toponyms.

sound_changes: Greek nominal endings adapt to Akkadian: -os>-u (potamos>potamu-class), -on>-u or >0, -e>-u; very short or vowel-final Greek roots take Akkadian -u/-um; case-vowel and mimation pattern of Akkadian imposed
Greek aspirates and clusters retained as a learned overlay (th, ph, kh, st, pr, kl) but fitted to Akkadian syllable shape; Greek pitch-accent replaced by Akkadian penultimate stress
Akkadian emphatics/gutturals (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts) and triconsonantal roots dominate; Akkadian construct chains (Bit-, Dur-, Kar-) and -tu/-um inflection are the productive morphology
retain the Akkadian sh/q/kh and the Greek th/ph; deep a/i/u vowels favored over Greek o where they collide; signature phonemes of both ancestries kept audible
fusion_rules.source_tilt: sea/civic/learned/material/trade words from Hellenic roots (the polis, agora, thalassa, marble, the learned overlay), each filtered to Akkadian shape; rule/kin/temple/land/staple words from Akkadian roots (the construct-city, the bit-ili, the alluvial field, the scribal backbone); every root then run through the one Akkadian-dominant sound-law so the seam is invisible

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Akkadian rule/kin/temple/land-roots + Hellenic sea/civic/learned/material-roots, all run through one Akkadian-dominant sound-law (Greek -os/-on endings adapted to -u/penultimate stress, aspirates and clusters retained as a learned overlay); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. No slashes - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Akkadian backbone keeps the 'mar-' (son of) patronymic and theophoric constructs; the Greek dynastic stock carry a -ides/-id- patronymic and a polis-demonym of origin; the throne fuses both - a basileus-house that also carries a Bit- house-name and a mar- lineage.
morphology.compounding_rule: Akkadian construct-chains (Bit-[god], Dur-[ruler], Kar-[god]) layered over Greek learned-compounds with linking -o- adapted to a consonant-final or -u root (Neapolu, Megapolu): the capital Hellashur (Hellas-of-Ashur), Dur-Seleku (fort of the ruling house), Alpolu-Tullaru (the polis-city of Tullaru).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Hellenistic dynasty over the Akkadian temple-cities: the basileus and his diadochoi-kin at the crown, the Greek strategoi and the Akkadian shaknu-governors over the alu-cities and the poleis, the gymnasion and the agora beside the ziggurat and the bit-ili; the sangu-priesthood and the scribal shatammu serve beneath. Polis/republican forms are aesthetic flavor, not modeled.)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Akkadian ladder, ascending, dominant; the Greek civic register stands beside it as the polis-administration. Hazannu (mayor) barony; Massaru (warden) march; Shaknu (appointed governor) county - shown in English as 'Archon', the approved Greek polis-magistrate term, the visible mark of the Hellenistic graft; Turtanu (commander-in-chief) duchy; Rubu (prince) principality; Sharru (king) kingdom over a Sharrutu; Shar-kishshati (king of the totality; Akk) empire over the Kishshatu. The Greek strategos (general-governor) and the polis-archon serve as co-titles beneath the Akkadian crown; the sangu (priest) and scribal shatammu stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Akkadian and Greek registers (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Mar-Sharri (son of the king; the crown prince; the Greek register names him Diadochos)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler' - here 'Archon' at the county tier). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Akkadian backbone stock carry a theophoric given name + mar- patronymic; the Greek dynastic stock carry a personal name + -ides patronymic + polis-demonym; order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Akkadian city-folk keep theophoric names (X-iddina, Warad-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the Greek dynastic and learned class keep Hellenic names (Tulrio-, -ides, polis-demonyms); the throne carries both - a basileus with a Bit- house-name.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Akkadian devotional constructs on the morphed canon-stems: Warad-Tullaru (servant of Tullaru), Tullaru-iddina (Tullaru-gave-me); Hellenic devotional on the morph variants: Tulrio-, Orlandro-.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Akkadian reflexes PRIMARY (family_near_eastern / hammuran morphs: Tullaru, Urlandu, Gayandu, Numunu, Rialtu, Itarnu), Hellenic morph variants SECONDARY (family_classical / achillean: Tulrios, Orlandros, Numenos), never real Mesopotamian or Greek gods. All three alignments: the Akkadian law-stele tradition meets the Greek civic cult of the polis.
religion.the_one: Itarnu (Akkadian; Hellenic Aiternos) - the great distant Ancient One, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tullaru (Hellenic Tulrios) - the sun and judgment

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Itarnu, Tullaru the just, Urlandu of the sworn war, Rialtu the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers lemnu (evil ones) or daimones, warded; the law-stele and the polis-oath bind alike
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the deified law-givers and city-founders (the heroes inscribed on the stele and honored at the heroon) and the city-spirits of the bit-ili; the great powers invoked at the temple and the temenos situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Itarnu - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as lemnu (Akkadian evil) or daimones (Hellenic), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakshu the City-Burner (Hellenic Maraxos the Tyrant-Flame); Vacidus -> Bakidu-lemnu the Unmaking; Lusanto -> Lusantu the Hoard-Worm.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bit-ili (Akkadian god-house) or Temenos (Hellenic sacred-precinct) of [power]: 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru', 'the Temenos of Tulrios'.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified law-givers of the cities and the Heros [name] (deified founder), inscribed on the stele and honored at the ziggurat and the heroon.
